cultural.vision_reason: This is a woven ulos textile with indigo warp-faced ground, tapestry-woven end bands with diamond, zigzag and cross motifs, and beaded fringe—the classic form of Batak ceremonial cloth from Sumatra, matching the claimed ethnicity and category.

physical.title: cloth
physical.summary: Cloth, an 'ulos'; large and rectangular; made from two equal sized pieces of (predominantly) dark blue (indigo dyed) warp faced tabby cotton (possibly another fibre, as the yarn is rough) cloth (sewn together edge to edge along one selvedge), with identical patterning at each end.  Unadorned centre field (some indigo worn away).  Diamond, zigzag, cross and indented motifs and patterning in bands towards each warp end, and in composite stripes at selvedges.  Worked in a variety of techniques; dicontinuous supplementary warp ('jugia') and weft and tapestry weave, using natural cream, tones of brown and black cotton yarns.  A separate woven band at fell of cloth, using the cloth's warp as weft.  These warp ends (like the main warp) plied and suspended with polychrome, black, white and transparent glass beads (beadwork), some fringes partially covered with folded stripes of metal.  Threaded white, red/brown and black beads stitched to selvedges; those beside patterned bands forming a zigzag patterning, with small strips of scarlet broadcloth (trade cloth, wool) at outer edge.  Two lines of red flannel strips stitched at each end (on both sides).  Patterning reversible.  Vestiges of pieces of paper stuck to one side of cloth.
